plans.note: Look for any liability cap / consequential damages waiver in the indemnification article (Art. 12) or the disclaimer at 13.6; if only a warranty disclaimer exists and no mutual monetary cap, treat as missing rather than deviation. Note PB's exposure is largely the payment/buy-out mechanics in Art. 6, which is capped separately.

Article 12 is the indemnification and insurance article. Check that SFJ indemnifies PB (PB Indemnified Parties) for third-party claims arising from SFJ's acts, and that PB's indemnity to SFJ Indemnified Parties is not open-ended for all Clinical Trial/product liability without fault carve-outs.

Defined terms 'Competing Product', 'Brilinta Competing Product', 'Generic Ticagrelor Product' and 'Exclusive Period' signal a restriction on PB developing or commercializing competing products; locate the operative covenant (likely in the definitions-linked covenant in Art. 2/3 or the miscellaneous/covenant provisions) and assess scope and duration against the rule.

Check the 'Exclusive Period' and 'Approved CRO'/'Approved Vendor'/'Permitted Third Party' constructs in Art. 3 for obligations forcing PB to use only SFJ-approved suppliers or to refrain from Licensing Transactions; also review the Licensing Transaction definition (1.1.117) and any consent gates.

No MFN-style 'best terms' language is signalled by the outline; closest analogues are the Licensing Transaction and payment/buy-out provisions. Confirm no covenant obliges PB to extend SFJ terms no less favourable than those given to third parties before marking missing/not applicable.

No non-solicitation defined term or heading appears; sweep the miscellaneous article and the confidentiality article for an employee non-solicit binding PB. If present, check duration and general-advertising carve-out.

Article 14 (Term and Termination) governs. Assess whether PB has any exit right (buy-out/Program Transfer or Change of Control Buy-Out Payment) and whether SFJ can walk away mid-development (e.g., on Material Adverse Event, Going Concern Notice, or failure of Phase 3 Success Criteria); note any exit is priced via Buy-Out Payment rather than free notice.

Term is likely tied to the Development Program/Approval Payment obligations rather than a renewing subscription term; confirm no evergreen renewal or price-uplift mechanic in Art. 14 and the 'Term'/'Development Term' definitions before recording as not applicable.

Governing law, Dispute resolution and Executive Officers escalation should sit in Article 15. Confirm the chosen law is New York/Delaware/California/England & Wales and whether disputes go to courts or to arbitration (and if arbitration, its seat).

Check the assignment clause in Art. 15 for PB's ability to assign to Affiliates and to a successor, and cross-check the 'Change of Control' definition, the Change of Control Buy-Out Payment in Art. 6/14, and the encumbrance covenants at 7.5.3 which may function as an indirect consent gate.

Article 11 covers Intellectual Property and Personally Identifiable Information. Verify PB owns Trial Inventions, Research Results, Clinical Trials Database and Regulatory Documentation, and that no assignment of PB Intellectual Property or trial data runs to SFJ (security interest in Art. 7 aside).

Identify the licence PB receives or grants (Licensed Patents/Licensed Know-How, AstraZeneca Product references, AZ License pass-throughs) in Art. 11 and any Program Transfer licence on termination in Art. 14; confirm any licence to PB extends to Affiliates and permitted contractors and is not revocable at will.

Article 9 (Records) plus the affirmative covenants at 7.6 are the likely audit/inspection hooks against PB. Check notice, frequency, business-hours limits, who bears cost, and whether SFJ's inspection rights extend to Sites and financial records.

Assess whether Approval Payments, Buy-Out Payment, Change of Control Buy-Out Payment or Timeline Remediation Plan consequences operate as penalties on PB versus agreed return-on-investment consideration; only flag genuine penalty/acceleration mechanics not already handled under T4C.

Article 13 holds the representations and warranties; 13.6 is the all-caps disclaimer. Confirm SFJ gives performance warranties for SFJ Services (conduct in accordance with SOPs, Applicable Law, ICH/GCP) and that 13.6 does not disclaim them entirely as against PB.

Insurance sits with indemnification in Article 12. Check whether the obligation is mutual or falls only on PB, and note limits/types; a PB-only obligation is consistent with the funding structure but confirm SFJ carries cover for its own personnel and services.

Article 4 (Development Costs, Maximum Development Costs, PB Costs) and Article 6 (payments to SFJ) are the spend-commitment provisions; assess whether PB is locked into funding or purchase obligations (e.g., Product Supply Costs, Approved Third Party Vendor Costs) without an exit, and avoid double-flagging the buy-out economics covered under T4C/LD.

Look for the Program Transfer / Program Transfer Agreement and effects-of-termination provisions in Art. 14, plus return or destruction of Confidential Information (Art. 10) and access to the Clinical Trials Database/Master File; confirm PB retains data and receives wind-down cooperation, and that transfer obligations running to SFJ are limited to a defined transition.
